If you refuse a request or demand, you do not give your permission for it; you withhold it.

ko: 관심을 갖고 눈여겨 봄, 주시, 주목, 고려.
en: If you have regard for something, you respect it.
Regard is how something is though about or looked at.
You use Regards as a closing in a formal letter.

ko: 거부하다; 생각이나 계획 따위에 동의하지 않다.
en: If you reject an idea or belief, you decide that you do not believe it.
If you reject a person, you refuse to care for that person.
If you reject an object, you refuse to take it or keep it.
If someone releases something, they let go of it; they stop holding it and set it free (let it be free).
Someone releases something when they put it out into the world (discharge it).
A company releases something when they let the public start using it.

ko: ~ (against something) (법률) (권리 침해에 대한 법적) 구제 방법
en: A remedy is something that corrects or counteracts something.
A remedy is a treatment, medicine, or application that cures a sickness or disease.
If you remit money, you send money to someone.
If you remit something, you stop the enforcement of a punishment.
If you repay a person, you pay them back the money they paid you in the past.
If you reply to someone or something, you answer using words.
If you reply to someone or something, you react.
If you rerun something, you run it again.
If you rerun a show, you broadcast it again.
If you reserve a room, a table, seat etc. you arrange for it to be kept for you, usually for a particular date and time.
When you're cooking, if you reserve something, you put it aside to use later.
If you reserve something for a particular situation, you usually don't use it except in that situation.
If you reset something you change it back to the way it started. You set it to the beginning again.
The past tense and past participle of reset.
If something or someone resides somewhere, it lives there or is located there.

ko: ㉹ (다른 대안이 없어서, 특히 좋지 못한 것에) 기대다[의지하다]
en: To choose to do something you don't want to do because you have no other choice.
To sort something again.
The solution of a mathematical equation.
The situation at the end of a process, its outcome.
If x results in y, it leads to or causes y.
If x results from y, it comes for or is caused by y.
If you retain something, you keep it.
If you retain someone (usually a professional), you pay them to do a job.
If you retire, you stop working, usually because of your age.
If you retire something, you stop using it.
If you retire, you go to a quiet place, often to bed.
If you reverse something, you make it act or move opposite to before (in the other direction).
Rhino is another way of spelling rhinoceros.
When you turn something right, you turn it the right-side-up.
When you make something right, you correct it.
Rigor is strict care and completeness in making sure something is correct.
The rigors of something are its difficult parts or its problems.
When a fruit or grain ripens, it becomes softer, sweeter, and ready to eat.
When a cheese ripens, it ages under controlled conditions and slowly develops its flavor, texture, and smell.
If something is risky, it is dangerous and involves risk.
Your rival is someone who is competing or fighting with you for the same thing; a competitor.
Someone or something with similar quality or distinction as another; an equal.
To oppose or compete with.
To equal or surpass another.
If something is done sadly, it is done in a sad manner.
If something is salty, it tastes of salt.
If a person or a person's speech is salty, it includes a lot of bad words or talk about sex.
If you sample something, you try or test a small amount of it.
If someone or something scares a person, it makes them feel fear.
If something scares a person off, it makes them not want to do something.
If a person scares up something, they find it, even though it's rare or hard to find.
Scary means a person or thing that scares someone.
A scent is a smell.
If x sents y, x gives y a smell.
If you scent something such as danger or a story, you have a feeling that it exists.
If an animal scents something, it smells it.

ko: <불가산> [the나 a 없이 쓰여] 학교 공부, 학교 생활.
en: A school is a place where you go to learn.
A school is a group of fish.
When you scold someone, you angrily tell them that they are doing something bad.
To gain points in a game, so that your score is increased.
To get a certain result on a text or quiz.
To have sex.
A scrap of paper or fabric is a small piece that is left unused after something is made.
A scrap of food is something that isn't eaten
Scrap metal or parts are pieces of junk that can be reused.
If you scratch you use a sharp object to make a mark on another object.
If you scratch you rub a part of your body, because you feel an itch.

ko: 소리치다, 외치다. 말, 웃음을 크게 터뜨리다.
en: If you scream, you yell or shout loudly.
If you scream, you move quickly; you race.

ko: (영화, 텔레비전, 컴퓨터 모니터 따위의) 화면, 영사면.
en: A screen is a flat surface for showing pictures, text or video.
A screen is a flat surface between two areas, often letting something in but keeping something out.
When someone searches for something, they don't know where it is and they look in many places to try to discover where it is.
A second is 1/60 of a minute. Sixty seconds is one minute.
If you select something, you choose it.
Sense is the ability to understand a situation or emotions.

ko: 연속. (소설, 영화, 드라마 따위) 연재물, 연속극.
en: A serial is a story or play appearing in pieces on a radio or magazine.
A series of events, meetings, experiments, etc. is several of them that happen one after the other and are related.
A TV or Radio series is a number of programs usually with the same setting and characters.
A series is a sporting event in which many teams compete for a championship.
If something is shaded, it is shielded from light.
If something is shading, it is approaching something slightly.
If you shade something in a drawing, you darken it.
If you shadow someone, you follow them closely without their knowing it.
If something is being shadowed, it is being covered in shadow or made dark.
If you shadow someone, you accompany them when they are working so as to learn about an occupation you intend to take up.
A shake is a type of beverage.
A shake is when something shakes.
If you shame someone, you make them feel shame.
A shark is a type of fish. Some are dangerous to humans, for example the great white shark, while others are not.
A blade, especially a sword used in fencing, with a sharp tip.
A sharp is a note that is one half step above the one that is named.
When you shave hair, you remove all of it with a sharp object such as a razor.
When you shave meat, you cut it into very thin slices.
To cut or trim something, especially using scissors or shears (tool).
To remove the fleece from a sheep etc. by clipping.
A sheep is an animal that people keep on farms and eat for food.
A sheep is a person who follows orders blindly and cannot think for themself.
Sheer is total, complete, without anything to hold it back.
Something that is sheer is very steep, almost vertical.
Sheer material is so thin you can almost see through it.
A shift is a movement.
A shift is the time that workers start and finish work.
The shift key on a computer changes from small to big letters.
A shirt is a piece of clothing you wear on the upper part of your body. Shirts are not very thick.
If a person shivers, they shake when they are cold or frightened.
If you shout, you speak very loudly.
A shrew is a very small, mouse-like mammal with a long pointed snout. Despite its appearance, it is not a mouse and belongs to a different group of mammals.
A shrew is a woman who is always angry and complains too much.

ko: (특정인을 기리는) 신성한 장소; 성전, 성지, 신전, 사당, 성당
성물이나 성인의 유해를 보관하고 있는 상자
en: A shrine is a holy or sacred place dedicated to a certain deity or a person who is respected.
A sieve is a device with a mesh bottom to separate larger particles from smaller ones, or to separate solids from a liquid.
If you sieve something, you put it through a sieve.
When you sight something, you see it.
In baseball if you single, you hit the ball and are able to run to first base.
If you single something out, you identify it, often to give it special attention.
If you siphon something, you transfer liquid through a siphon.
If you siphon something, you steal in small amounts.
To skate is to travel using roller skates, ice skates, or a skate board.
Being able to do something well. Unlike abilities, skills must usually be learned.
A skunk is an animal that releases a strong odor when frightened.
Slang is an informal way of speaking that is used mostly within certain social groups.
To work very hard.
Sleep is the activity or time of resting quietly with eyes shut, usually in bed for many hours at night.
If you sleep, you rest quietly with eyes shut, usually in bed for many hours at night.
If you sleep with someone, you have sex with them.
A slope is one side of a hill.
The slope of a line is how far up it goes divided by how far along it goes.
A slope is an extremely offensive word for an Asian.
A slump is a sudden fall of something, especially for an extended period.
A small person or thing is not big. It doesn't have much size.
The way a thing smells; the substance in the air that people can smell.
To put one's mouth in a form which shows that one is happy; to have the sides of one's mouth higher than the middle.
If you snake, you move in a winding path.
If you snake, you clean or unclog a clog using a plumbing snake.
If something gets snared, it gets trapped in a snare.
If you snatch something from a person, you take it from them in a quick and rude way.
If you sneak, you walk into a place quietly, usually to avoid being noticed by other people of that place.
An act of breathing to find out what the smell is.
If a person or animal snores, they breathe during sleep with a harsh, snorting noises that is caused by an obstruction in air movement.
A snowy plot of land is covered with snow.
If you solve a problem, you fix it or deal with it.
If you solve a question, you find a correct answer.
The direction opposite to north. For a person looking at the setting sun, the south is on their left hand.

ko: 예비 또는 비축해 둔 것, 여분
en: A spare is an extra thing, such as a key, just in case it is needed.
A spare is a tire that you keep in your car in case one of the other tires has a problem.
A spear is a long stick that is sharp at one or both ends and is used as a weapon.
A spear is a piece of asparagus or other vegetables that looks like a spear.
The speed of something is how fast it moves.
When you speed, you move or do something very fast.
When you speed in a car, you drive faster than the law allows.

ko: 철자하다, (낱말을) 맞춤법에 따라 쓰다, 철자를 말하다.
en: To make up a word.
To say or write all the letters that make up a word, in the right order.
To spell all the words in a language correctly.
A sphere is a shape that is round in all directions, like a ball. Every point on a sphere is the same distance from the centre (a point in the middle) of the sphere.
If you spirit something, you carry it away, usually in secret or mystery.
When two people spoon, they lie next to each other with one person's back against the other person's front, similar to the way two spoons are stacked together.
If something springs, it jumps quickly and far.

ko: (약어:sq) (면적을 나타낼 때에는 숫자 뒤에 써서) 제곱/평방의
en: If something is square, it is shaped like a sqaure.
If something is stable, it is unlikely to move or change.
If you are stable, you are calm and don't get upset easily.
A stable is a building for housing animals like horses and cows.

ko: 교착 상태에 빠뜨리다, 지연시키다; 교착 상태에 빠지다, 지연되다
en: If something stalls, it stops improving or progressing.
If an engine or vehicle stalls, it stops working because there is too much load and not enough fuel.
If you stall, you purposefully slow things down or make people wait because you're not ready.

ko: 눈을 동그랗게 뜨고 처다보다. 뚫어지게 들여다 보다.
en: When someone is looking at you for a very long time, he is staring at you.

ko: (특정한 서비스가 제공되거나 이루어지는 장소·건물. 상점, 방송국 따위 지역 영업소) 소, 국, 부서.
en: A station is a place where many trains or buses stop and people buy tickets and get on.
A station is a place where a person stays in one place and works.
A stead is a place or spot.
To prevent something from falling, make something stable.
If you steal, you take somebody's money or things without their permission.
If you steal a base you run to it before the ball was hit.
A very strong metal made of iron and other substances mixed together.
A steer is a young bull or ox that has been castrated and raised for beef.
Now like in the past.
A sting is a pointed item at the rear of an insect, for defence.
A sting can also mean a bite by an insect.
A sting is a bump on the skin, the result of being stung.
To sting means to inject venom with a stinger.
to sting means to hurt or bite.
To swindle or con. (metaphor)
If something stinks, it has a strong bad smell to it.

ko: (상점 등에) (물품을) 들여놓다, 사들이다, 재고품으로 쌓아 두다 (with);(상품 등을) 비축하다, 저장하다.
en: If a store stocks a product, it has it available to be sold.
If you stock x with y, you fill x with y.
If you stock up on something, you get more than you use in a short time.
If you stoop, you bend your head and shoulders forward.
If you stoop, you lower your moral standard by doing something that is below one's status.
If a bird stoops, it flies of glides downwards suddenly.
To store something is to put something away, usually if it is not being used.
A stork is a large wading bird with long legs and a long beak of the family Ciconiidae.
A stork is a mythical bringer of babies to families, or good news.
If you storm, you move fast and noisily like a storm, usually when angered.
If you storm a building or other fortification, you assault it with military troops.
If something is stout, it is big and strong.
If you stray, go do not do something the normal way; you wander.
If something streams, it comes in a flow, usually in order and often not stopping.
When you hit something, you strike it.
When an idea strikes you, it occurs to you suddenly or with force.
When a clock rings a bell to tell you the time, the clock strikes the time.
A stroke is when blood stops coming into your brain.
A stroke is an action of hitting something lightly.
A stroke is the person who sets the speed in a rowing crew.
If you style something, you design and make it appear in a certain way.
If you subdue a situation, you overcome or bring it under control.
If someone or something is subject to something, they are likely to be affected by it or experience it.
A subject is a branch of knowledge in school, college or university, such as English, math, science, and history.
In English grammar, the subject of a sentence is usually a noun that comes before the verb. This noun is usually the thing that is doing the action, and it is usually the topic of the sentence.
A subject is a person who is governed by a king, queen, emperor, etc.
If you submit something, usually a piece of writing, you give it to somebody to be checked or accepted.
If you submit to some authority, you accept that they have power over you.

ko: (타) 추측하다, 암시하다 (to imply but stop short of saying explicitly.)
en: If a person says an option, he or she is suggesting.
A survey is a broad look at a topic or place.
A survey is a formal way to gather data by asking question of people: a questionnaire.
A land survey involves photographing and measuring the land to make a map of it.
If you survive something, you experience it and you did not die.
If you suspend something, you stop it for a time.
If you suspend someone from a job or from school, you stop them from going for a time.
If you suspend an object, you attach it above and hang it down.
When you swear, you say a swear word.
When you swear, you make a promise or an oath.
A salty water that is produced naturally by the body.
A natural occurrence of the body to allow the body to cool by excreting salty water (see above).
When you sweep the floor, you use the broom to clean it.
A sweet is a piece of candy.
When something swells, it becomes larger, usually due to an increase in blood in an area of the body.
A system is a group of things that work together; a way of doing something.
Something that is taboo is considered forbidden, or is at least strongly discouraged.
If you taint something, you contaminate or pollute it.
A tarmac is a mixture of tar and very small stones, it is used for making roads.
If you tarmac something, you cover it with tarmac.
To help someone learn something. To tell someone how to do something.
An act of making fun of somebody. Usually for enjoyment and is not a personal attack.
If you tease a person, you entice or tempt them.

ko: <돈을> 지불하다, (채무 변제로서) <돈·물품을> 제공하다.(to offer a payment, as at sales or auctions. )
en: to formally offer or show something to someone.
to make a formal offer to do a job or provide goods or services for a particular price.

ko: (재무) 채권(債券)의 만기까지의 기간 〔Time to maturity of a bond.〕
en: A tenor is the highest male vocal range, higher than bass or baritone.
A tenor is a musical instrument that is higher than a baritone, but lower than an alto.
A tenor is a singer who sings in the tenor range.
To say a good word after someone gives something to you or after someone does something good for you.

ko: 가산 (사실・사건・상황・행동 등을 가리키는) 것, 일; 말; 생각
en: A thing is something.
The plural form of thing; more than one (kind of) thing.
A third of something is one of three equal parts of that thing.
Thirst is the feeling that you want to drink.
Thirst is the state of not having enough to drink.
If you have a thirst for something, you want a lot of it regularly.
To thrive is to grow or develop well or vigorously.
When you throw an object, you make it fly through the air using your hands.
A tiger is a mammal. It comes from Asia.
If a person is timid, he or she does not have the courage or confidence to complete something.
To give a title to someone or something.
Today is the current day, the day that is happening now, the day between yesterday and tomorrow.
Today is modern times; the present in general.
A tooth is a hard, white thing in your mouth. You use your teeth to chew food.
A tooth is a sharp point sticking out of something and forms a row of sharp objects for cutting.
A tooth is a rounded point on a gear that is used to transmit or receive force and motion to other gears.
A topic is a general idea that someone is speaking (reading, thinking, etc.) about at a specific time.
A total is the final amount of something. It is a term used in math.
If you total something, you add them up.
If something totals something, it adds up to that; it amounts to.
If you total something, you destroy it; you wreck it.
A toxin is a toxic substance that is produced by the biological processes of organisms.
If you trace something, you follow information to find where it came from or where it went.
If you trace a line, you draw it.
If you trace a picture or a shape, you draw it by putting a piece of paper over it and drawing what you see underneath.
When two people trade, one gives something to the other and the other gives something to the first one. They make an exchange. Sometimes money is one of the things.
When an event is tragic, it is causing a lot of pain and suffering for those involved in that event. We would call such event a tragedy as well.
A long vehicle with many cars that are joined together. A train runs on a track.
If you train someone, you teach them a particular skill.
To tread is to take a step.
To tread is to stand on, or crush.
The past tense and past participle of tread.
A trend is a general movement or change in one direction.

ko: 경향이 있다. 경향을 띠다. 경향을 취하다; 유행하다.
en: If something trends in one direction, it generally moves or changes in that direction.
If a you trickle a liquid, you pour it in a very thin stream.

ko: (신조어) 부정적이거나 선동적인 글 및 댓글을 인터넷에 게재하는 사람
en: A monster in stories that looks something like a human but a different size, and very ugly, that lives in caves or hills or under bridges.
A person who posts a comment to try to make other people angry and to cause trouble (drama and disruption).

ko: 폐를 끼치다, 성가시게 하다, 난처하게 하다.
en: To bother or annoy.
If you truck something, you send it somewhere on a truck
If you are trucking you are driving a truck. This usually means driving a big truck for a long way, and as a job.
If you are trucking you are going somewhere and are moving fast.
You use truly before an adjective to emphasize that something it has all the characteristics of that adjective.
You use truly to emphasize that you are speaking truthfully, that you really meaning it.
When you trust someone, you do not doubt them. You believe that someone is honest and will not cause harm. You believe you can rely on them.
If something is undue, it is excessive or more than what is needed.

ko: (타동사: ~ something)(...에서) 짐을 내리다.(To remove the load or cargo from (a vehicle, etc.).)
(타동사: ~ something (from something)) (자동차・선박 등에서) (짐을) 내리다 (To remove (the load or cargo) from a vehicle, etc. )
en: If you unload something, you remove the cargo from a vehicle.
If a vehicle is being unloaded, its cargo is being removed.
If you unload your anger, you vent or express it.
Upset means to be very angry or sad; to be unhappy.
Something is upset if it is in turned in the wrong direction like something that was dropped; turned in a direction with the bottom part up and the top part down.
A disturbance or disruption.
An unexpected win.
Utter is total or complete.
When something is vacant, it is unused, unoccupied or empty.
If something is vague, then it is not very clear or precise.
If something is valid, it is correct, appropriate, and acceptable.
If you value someone or something, you think that they are good and you don't want to lose them.
If you value something judge how good or important it is.
The verge of something its edge.
If something is "on the verge" of happening, it is very close to starting. (This expression is often used when something bad or dangerous is about to happen.)
The act of visiting.
To say a thought, articulate.
If something is vulgar, it is obscene or offensive.
If something is vulgar, it lacks sophistication or good taste.
If something is vulgar, it is ordinary.

ko: (비유) 정해진 상대 없이 아무나와 성관계를 하다. 바람을 피다.
en: When you wander around, you walk or move slowly around without a purpose.
Things that are not useful; things that people want to take out of their house.
If you water something, you add water to soil around plants.
If you water something, you give water to animals.
If you water something, you dilute it.
Human or artificial hair that is worn to change your appearance, either in addition to or by covering the natural hair altogether.
­A type or way of weaving.
Very strange or unusual. Very different from others of its kind or what is expected. Something that is weird is not at all normal.
A whale is a large animal that lives in the ocean.

ko: 비난하다, 좋지 않게 말하다, 투정하다, 헐뜯다.
en: If you whine, then you complain about something, usually childishly.
A woman who does witchcraft (magic) or has magical powers.
A person of either sex (man or woman) who does witchcraft.
Someone who practice traditional British magic (witchcraft).
If you witness something, you see it.
If something witnesses something, it experiences it.
A female human.
If you wonder about something, you think about it because you want to know more about it.
You use "wonder if/whether" to ask for or suggest something.
If you don't wonder something, you expect it.
If A worsens B, A makes B worse.
If something worsens, it becomes worse.
The superlative form of bad; most bad.
A wound is a cut in skin with pain and blood, a burn, or other similar mark on someone's body.
The past tense and past participle of wind.
If you wring something from somebody, you get it from them after hard bargaining.
If you wring (out) something wet, you squeeze or twist it tightly to force out the liquid in it.
If you wring your hands, you rub them together because you're worried about something.
A subject in school where you write stories and poems.
If something is wrong, it is not right. If something is wrong it may be incorrect, not true, or bad.
If something is wrong, it is not moral.
A wrong is an immoral act.
A young is an offspring of an animal.

ko: 주판. 작은 구슬들을 막대기에 꿰어 계산을 하기 위해 만든 나무 틀.
en: An abacus is an ancient calculating device. It is made of a frame with beads on various rods.
If you abduct a person, you take them away by force.
If things abound, or if a place abounds with things, there are very large numbers of them.
To abridge something is to make it shorter or less.
If something is absorbed, it is sucked or soaked up (usually a liquid).
If you absorb something, you take it in and use it; you learn it.
If something absorbs your time, it takes all it up; it occupies all of your time.
An accent is the particular way that somebody's speech sounds.
: This short entry needs someone to make it better. You can help Wiktionary by adding to it.

ko: (일, 목적) 이루다(뜻대로 되어 바라는 결과를 얻다.), 달성하다, 성취하다.
en: If you achieve success or a goal, you have completed what you planned to do or have a good result.
If you acquire something, you buy or get it.
The acerage of a property is the area in acres that it covers.
Somebody's acerage is their large property, often a farm.
If something is adamant, it is not easy to change.
If you addict someone or something, you make them become addicted to something, usually a harmful drug.
If you are addicted to something, you do it to the exclusion of everything else.
If one thing adjoins another, they touch each other. They are adjacent to one another.
If you adjust something, you change it a little so that it fits or works better.
If you adjust, you change the way you behave or think to suit a new situation.
If something is in advance of something else, it is before it.
An advance is a move forward.
An advance is an amount of money given to someone before they normally get it.
If you advance something, you bring or move it forward.
If you advance someone some money, you pay it to them before they would normally get it.
An adverb is a kind of word that generally modifies verbs and other words (but not nouns); adverbs usually answer questions such as how?, why? and to what extent?.
If you allude to something, you bring it up without actually saying it.
